text.en:
When a bridge opened over the river near Meena's village, buses began to reach the town in half the time.
Her father said, "Roads, bridges and electricity change how people live and work."

Infrastructure means the basic structures and services a country needs: roads, railways, ports, airports, electricity, water supply and communication networks such as the telephone and internet.
India's first passenger train ran from Bombay to Thane in 1853. Today the Indian Railways is among the largest networks in the world. National highways such as the Golden Quadrilateral join the big cities. Ports carry goods by sea and airports link cities and countries.
Good infrastructure helps farmers sell crops, children reach school, factories get power and people get jobs. Building it costs a lot and must take care of the environment.

problem.en: How does a new road help a village?

text.en: Farmers can take crops to the market quickly.
Children and doctors can travel easily.

prompt.en: A friend says infrastructure is only for cities. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Villages need roads and power too.
It helps farmers and schools everywhere.

points.en: Infrastructure includes roads, rail, ports, airports, power and communication.
The first passenger train ran in 1853.
It helps development but must protect the environment.
